summary.text: The domain behind your published company email lapses soon, so your quotes and invoices will bounce — and anyone can already send mail that looks like yours.
Your head-office phone, email and branch list differ across your own sites and listings, so a customer ready to enquire can reach the wrong line or inbox.
Your Google rating of 4.7 from 32 reviews is a real asset, yet none of your newest reviews has a reply from you.

titles.f1: The domain behind your company email lapses soon. Quotes and tender mail sent there will bounce.
titles.f2: Anyone can send email that looks like it comes from you, so a forged invoice can reach your clients in your name.
titles.f3: On a phone your site shows nothing for seconds, and that is where most homeowners first meet you.
titles.f4: A search-engine check fails on your homepage, so new project and credential pages are slower to appear in search.
titles.f5: Prospects see an unanswered low rating at the top of your Google profile and no reply from you on the newest reviews.
titles.f6: Your LinkedIn phone field holds nothing dialable, so a partner or recruiter who clicks call gets no answer.
titles.c1: Your head-office phone differs across your own sites and listings; a missed call at the quotation stage is a lost project.
titles.c2: You publish two different contact emails, so enquiries split and one inbox can go unanswered.
titles.c3: Your two sites list different branches, so a customer near a branch you run sees none on one of them.
titles.c4: Your head-office address is written two different ways, so couriers, auditors and site visits can reach the wrong unit.
titles.c5: Your staff count differs by a wide margin between your site and a public profile, weakening the scale you claim in tenders.
titles.c6: Every channel names a different one of your sites as official, so your newest credentials and project pages stay unseen.
titles.n1: A blank low rating carries the name of one of your engineers; worth checking, with nothing proven.
titles.n2: Clusters of top reviews land on the same days; worth watching before a rival points at them.
titles.n3: Your headline project and revenue figures appear only on your own pages, so a bank or tender panel cannot verify them.
titles.n4: A solar directory still files you under small installations, which undercuts the scale you pitch for.
titles.n5: A third domain serves a copy of your site; worth checking who controls it before it confuses customers.
